correctness.rationale: For the original unweighted adjacency Hamiltonian of the five-vertex path, the five exact simple spectral projectors yield six real moment variables. The six entries (1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,2),(2,3) give a coefficient determinant sqrt(3)/972, hence the unique moment vector (-1/5,0,2/5,2/5,0,0). Exact substitution gives 1/5 in all 25 mixing entries. The independent torus densities (1-2cos(theta)/5-2cos(2theta)/5)/(2pi) and (1-2cos(2phi)/5)/(2pi) have strict positive bounds, reproduce the vector by Fourier orthogonality and yield a relative-interior barycenter. The irrational (sqrt(3),1) time flow is dense even after any threshold; convex relative-interior transfer and Caratheodory in affine dimension <=6 guarantee at most seven positive physical time atoms. verify.py recomputes spectral projectors, the full exact system and a separate quadrature. The convexity and density claims are analytic, not extrapolated from a grid.

value.rationale: This resolves the first case n=5 beyond the explicitly stated unweighted-path open problem n>=5, with a complete necessary-and-sufficient characterization of all admissible observation-time laws, a concrete strictly positive two-phase witness, a finite exact support bound of seven, and the ability to place every atom after any chosen threshold. Exact equality and common-law uniformity are stronger than near mixing on one row. No general n-path theorem, optimal sample count, or constructive schedule is claimed.
